summary: Klamath National Forest lookout on Cory Peak, manned in 1929 and 1930 per newspaper notices; listed gone; no build, type or removal date found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Fire Lookout Association, with type unknown; no date or cause of removal found

staffing.status: manned in 1929 and 1930 per newspaper notices quoted by Forest Lookouts; no later record found

events.note: October 1929 Siskiyou Daily News notice, quoted by Forest Lookouts, names Paul Friday as of the Cory lookout
July 1930 Siskiyou Daily News notice, quoted by Forest Lookouts, says Carl Utz and family moved up to the lookout for the summer

evidence.supports: Cory Peak is a mountain in the Klamath Mountains, about 7,746 feet high
evidence.quote: Cory Peak (2 361m/7 746ft a.s.l.) is a mountain in the Klamath Mountains in USA

evidence.supports: listed in Siskiyou and Trinity counties
agency listed as Klamath National Forest
October 3, 1929 notice names Paul Friday of the Cory lookout, who took over as fire guard at the Trumble ranch from Claude Tovrea
evidence.quote: October 3, 1929: Paul Friday of the Cory lookout took Claude Tovrea's place as fire guard at the Trumble ranch.

evidence.supports: July 3, 1930 notice: Carl Utz, his wife and two children moved up to the lookout for the summer
evidence.quote: July 3, 1930: Mr. and Mrs. Carl Utz, with their daughter, Doris, and son, Jerome, have moved up to the lookout at Cory peak, where Utz is stationed for the summer.

evidence.supports: listed as gone, type unknown, in Siskiyou/Trinity
evidence.quote: Cory Peak Siskiyou/ Trinity 41.32905 -122.60412 Unknown Gone

notes_for_editor: Both staffing items are newspaper notices quoted secondhand by Forest Lookouts (Siskiyou Daily News); the originals were not checked. The October 1929 notice may mean Friday was a fire guard at the Trumble ranch rather than at the lookout; the story now gives the notice's own wording (of the Cory lookout) and also reports the Trumble ranch post, so check it. No build date, design, access or removal detail was found in any source. The Siskiyou County page on Forest Lookouts lists Cory Peak under Klamath National Forest with a legal description only (40N-7W-18); not used. The brief record (kind unknown, gone, agency, county, coordinates) matches the sources; no corrections.
